simple.meaning: נְכֹת (nᵉkôth) is a Hebrew object word meaning “spicery , i.e. (generally) valuables.” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.
simple.biblicalBackground: The occurrence trail begins at 2 Kings 20:13. The background is built from the passages where the word occurs.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to נְכֹת (H5238) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Concrete words often carry patterns through Scripture because objects, animals, offerings, and created things are used repeatedly in worship, judgment, covenant, and narrative.
simple.summary: נְכֹת (nᵉkôth) / H5238 is traced through 2 Kings 20:13, Isaiah 39:2 with generated occurrence evidence.

definitions.full: H5238. nekoth [ נְכֹת ] noun [feminine] treasure (so context demands) ( ᵐ5 L 2Kin 20:13 τῆς ὑπάρξεως , compare ᵑ7 ᵑ6 ; derivation uncertain; Dl Prol. 141 compare Assyrian bit nakamti (nakanti) , house of treasure , √ nakâmu , heap up [Dl HWB 462 ], whence ׳ב ׳נ perhaps borrowed; this favoured by Nö ZMG xl (1886), 731 Hpt ZA ii. 256 (reading nakavâti = nakamâti , and Hebrew ׳ב נִכְוֺתָיו or ׳ב נְכוֺתָו )). — Only suffix נְכֹתֹה בֵּית = his treasure-house 20:13 = Isa 39:2 .
